candidate.statement: KMT2A-rearranged AML cell lines exhibit increased dependency on MEN1 (more negative dependency score) compared to KMT2A wild-type cell lines.
queries: MLL rearranged leukemia menin MEN1 CRISPR essential

review.rationale: The candidate asserts that KMT2A-rearranged AML cell lines exhibit increased dependency on MEN1 (more negative dependency score) compared to wild-type cell lines. Extensive functional and mechanistic evidence (e.g., MED:42278415, MED:41882099, MED:41799513, MED:42512270) establishes that KMT2A fusion oncoproteins require direct interaction with Menin (encoded by MEN1) to drive leukemogenesis and aberrant HOXA/MEIS1 transcriptional networks. MED:42278415 and MED:41882099 document that deletion/knockout or targeted perturbation of MEN1 selectively disrupts KMT2A-rearranged AML cell survival, leukemia maintenance, and induces myeloid differentiation, establishing a strong expected genetic dependency in KMT2A-rearranged AML versus wild-type lines.

candidate.statement: KMT2A-rearranged AML cell lines exhibit enhanced dependency on DOT1L compared to non-rearranged lines.
queries: MLL DOT1L essentiality acute myeloid leukemia

review.rationale: The candidate posits that KMT2A-rearranged AML exhibits enhanced dependency on DOT1L compared to non-rearranged AML lines (a well-established canonical epigenetic dependency in AML). Multiple retrieved sources document this specific relationship. For example, MED:41350360 details that KMT2A fusion proteins directly engage DOT1L via fusion partners (such as AF9, AF10, ENL) to hypermethylate H3K79 and sustain HOXA9/MEIS1 oncogenic programs, establishing DOT1L as a critical dependent target in KMT2A-rearranged AML. MED:42512270 and MED:41882099 further confirm that KMT2A-rearranged AML cells depend on DOT1L-mediated H3K79 methylation, where perturbation/inhibition of DOT1L selectively derepresses myeloid differentiation and reduces leukemic cell viability.
